annotations.title: Wholesale prices of live animals, fish, eggs and fresh food

description: Use this when a user asks what the wholesale price of live pigs, cattle or chickens, fish, eggs or other fresh food is today in Australia (country AU), Canada (country CA), Germany (country DE), France (country FR), England and Wales (country GB), Hong Kong (country HK), Malaysia (country MY) or United States (country US), or how it moved on the previous day. Returns the newest daily average reference wholesale price that the government publishes for the food type, per kilogram or per egg, with the day it applies to, the change on the previous published day, the recent days, the official source and licence. This is a posted reference price reported by wholesalers (price_type posted_price), not a paid price and not a range built from sales, so the range fields are null and there is no sample size. How fresh: Australia: daily on trading days (MLA updates at midnight AEST); every answer states the trading day it describes; Canada: weekly (a Friday date); our copy is refreshed daily and each answer states the week its quotes apply to; Germany: weekly (calendar week); each answer states the week its price applies to; France: daily on market days (each market line carries its own date); each answer states the dates its quotes apply to; England and Wales: about every two weeks (a Monday date); each answer states the date its price applies to; Hong Kong: daily on working days, published by the AFCD when necessary; each answer states the day its price applies to; Malaysia: monthly, not live: the catalogue is refreshed after each month closes (catalogue last updated 10 October 2026 when checked); our copy is refreshed daily and every answer names its month; United States: weekly, published on Monday for the week just ended; every answer states the report date. Do not use for supermarket or shop prices, for the price one farm received, for restaurant prices, for futures prices, or for other countries.

country.description: AU = Australia (Meat & Livestock Australia: daily weighted average saleyard auction prices for cattle and sheep, national indicators, not monthly); CA = Canada (AAFC weekly wholesale asking prices of fresh fruit and vegetables at Calgary, Edmonton, Vancouver and Winnipeg, quoted not paid); DE = Germany (BLE weekly national wholesale-market quotations for fruit and vegetables, quoted not paid); FR = France (FranceAgriMer RNM quotes of fruit and vegetables at producer markets, dispatch, import and wholesale, EUR excluding VAT per kg, quoted not paid, daily); GB = England and Wales (DEFRA average wholesale prices of home-grown fruit and vegetables at the Birmingham, Bristol, Manchester and London markets, quoted not paid, about every two weeks); HK = Hong Kong (AFCD daily average reference wholesale prices of fresh food, posted by wholesalers, not paid prices); MY = Malaysia (Department of Statistics Malaysia: monthly average fish and seafood prices per kg at landing, wholesale and retail, official statistic, not a live price); US = United States (USDA AMS: weekly average price packers paid for fed steers and heifers, negotiated cash purchases, national, not monthly)

level.description: Malaysia fish only: ex_vessel (the price fishers get at first sale at landing; default), wholesale or retail.

market.description: CA only: one wholesale centre (Calgary, Edmonton, Vancouver or Winnipeg). Leave out for all centres together. AAFC does not quote every centre every week (the latest file has only Calgary and Winnipeg); an unquoted centre answers with the list of centres that are quoted.

product.description: The food in plain words, e.g. 'live pig', 'chicken', 'eggs', 'grass carp', 'tomato'. The list for each country is in the tool notes. Australia: cattle or sheep in everyday words, e.g. cattle, western young cattle, restocker steers, feeder steers, steers, dairy cows, light lamb, lamb, heavy lamb, merino lamb, restocker lamb, mutton, restocker heifers, cows. Prices are Australian dollars: cents per kg (carcase or live weight, the answer says which) or dollars per head for the online indicators. The answer is for the newest trading day, not a month. CA: fresh fruit and vegetables such as apples, bananas, grapes, avocados, carrots, cabbage, cucumbers, celery, broccoli, cauliflower, beets, garlic, ginger, blueberries and Chinese vegetables. The answer is the median CAD per kg of the week's wholesale asking quotes with the 10th to 90th percentile and the number of quotes; add market=Calgary, Edmonton, Vancouver or Winnipeg for one centre. DE: fruit and vegetables on the German wholesale markets, in English or German: apples, pears, cucumbers, tomatoes, peppers, grapes, kiwis, plums, lemons, zucchini, oranges, mandarins, onions, aubergines, strawberries, cauliflower, carrots, peaches, nectarines, bananas, lettuce, leeks, brussels sprouts and more (no potatoes). A variety such as 'elstar' also works. The answer is the median of that week's national quotations in EUR per kg, with the cheapest and dearest quotation and the change on the previous week. FR: fruit and vegetables, English or French names: carrot, tomato, potato, onion, leek, cabbage, cauliflower, courgette, lettuce, apple, pear, orange, strawberry, peach, grape and about 60 more. The answer is the median of the quoted average prices per kg across the market lines of the last 7 days (retail, organic and bunch lines left out), with the lowest and highest quote and the markets. GB: home-grown fruit and vegetables: apples (gala, bramley, cox...), pears, plums, strawberries, raspberries, blackberries, blueberries, cherries, gooseberries, currants, carrots, onions, leeks, cauliflower, cabbage, calabrese, lettuce, tomatoes, cucumbers, courgettes, capsicum, beans, peas, beetroot, parsnips, swede, turnip, sprouts, celery, rhubarb, kale and more (no potatoes). An item with several varieties gives the mean of the varieties and lists each; add the variety (for example 'gala apples') for one price. Prices are GBP per kg, per head, per twin pack or per stem; the answer names the unit and the date. HK: live pig, live cattle, live chicken (local or mainland), eggs (mainland, USA, Germany), marine fish (golden thread, yellow croaker, mackerel, hairtail...), freshwater fish (grass carp, big head, mud carp) and vegetables (tomato, potato, broccoli, spinach, cabbage, Chinese kale, celery...). Prices are HK$ per kg (converted from per catty) or HK$ per egg; the answer names the unit and the day. Malaysia: a fish or seafood in English or Malay, e.g. mackerel, kembong, tenggiri, pomfret, bawal_putih, prawn, udang_harimau, squid, sotong_katak, crab, siakap, kerapu, bilis. About 150 kinds are published; a word that fits several (mackerel, prawn) returns the list to choose from. Prices are in ringgit per kg. United States: fed cattle in everyday words, e.g. cattle, steers, heifers, dressed steers, dressed heifers. Prices are US dollars per hundredweight (100 lb), live or dressed weight as the answer says. The answer is for the newest weekly report, not a month.

name: pricepaid_wholesale_fresh_food_prices

outputSchema.description: A price answer: a range or an official statistic with sample size, period, confidence, source and licence.

answer_id.description: Audit trail: a stable id (hash of source id, normalised query, data period and method_version). The same question on the same data gives the same id; keep it with the reasoning that used the figure.

as_of.description: When the answer was produced (ISO 8601); the snapshot date when the official source was down and the answer comes from our copy.

data_age_days.description: Whole days between data_as_of and retrieved_at; null when data_as_of is null.

data_as_of.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the newest data point behind the figure; null when unknown.

evidence.description: Audit trail: what kind of evidence the figure is.

label.description: Short name of the kind of evidence, e.g. 'Recorded sale prices', 'Official published average', 'Official published index', 'Posted shelf or pump price', 'Posted or listed price', 'Contract award value', 'Regulated reimbursement price'.

meaning.description: One sentence on what this kind of evidence does and does not establish.

extra.description: Source-specific details (for example cheapest stations). extra.stale is true when the answer comes from our copy of the source.

method_version.description: Audit trail: version of the way this source turns raw data into an answer (per source, default '1').

notice.description: Information, not a valuation or offer. Also says when the answer is our copy because the official source did not respond.

period.description: The period the records cover (ISO dates), or the date of the snapshot when the answer comes from our copy.

anyOf.description: The price. Null when there is not enough data to publish a figure (fewer than 5 records) or nothing matched.

measure.description: What value is: median for ranges built from records; average or median for official statistics.

typical_high.description: 90th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

typical_low.description: 10th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

unit.description: What the price is per, e.g. 'per litre', 'per home', 'per kWh'.

value.description: The headline figure. For ranges built from records it equals median.

price_type.description: transaction, posted_pump_price, posted_price, contract_price, reimbursement_price or official_statistic.

query.description: The request as understood, echoed back.

reliability.description: How far to trust the figure as a distribution of real prices. official_with_count = a published official figure with a record count; official_median_no_count = a published average or median with no record count (confidence 'high' there means the publisher is official, not that a count was checked); record_level = 15+ records we hold; thin = 5–14 records; stale = our copy because the official source did not respond; insufficient_data = no figure published.

retrieved_at.description: Audit trail: when ProofPrice produced this answer (ISO 8601). For an answer from our own copy this is now, while as_of is the snapshot date.

sample_size.description: Number of records behind the figure; null when the publisher does not say.

source.description: Where the figure comes from, under which licence, and the attribution line to show.

attribution.description: The attribution line to show with the figure.

url.description: The publisher's page for this data.

statistic.description: Official statistics only: what kind of figure it is and the period the publisher states it for.

status.description: ok = a figure is returned; insufficient_data = fewer than 5 matching records; no_matches = nothing matched.

suggestions.description: Short plain things to try next: widen the period or area, ask for an itemised quote. May be empty.

summary.description: One plain sentence an AI can quote.
